title: Velouté de champignons
subtitle: Silky French mushroom velouté
excerpt: A smooth, cream-enriched mushroom soup made by building a base of sautéed button mushrooms, onion, and white wine, then blending and finishing with crème fraîche and butter. Velvety, subtle, and deeply savoury.
sourceNotes: Velouté de champignons is a classic of French domestic and restaurant cooking. The dish appears in multiple French culinary references including Escoffier's Le Guide Culinaire (1903) and in Larousse Gastronomique (1938), both available as public-domain or widely-cited historical references.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze before adding the crème fraîche. Defrost, reheat gently, and stir in the crème fraîche just before serving.
recipe.batchNotes: Doubles well. Make the base in a large pot, blend in batches.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Can be made entirely the day before and gently reheated. Add a splash of stock or water if it has thickened on standing.

glossaryTerms.definition: A smooth, velvety soup or sauce. In French cooking, a velouté soup is made from a blended vegetable or seafood base enriched with cream or butter to give a silky texture. The word means 'velvety' in French.

content.text: is a smooth, blended soup finished with cream or butter. This version uses button mushrooms. It takes under 45 minutes and produces something silky and rich with very little effort.
Melt the butter in a large saucepan over medium heat. Add the onion and cook for 8 minutes, stirring occasionally, until soft and translucent. Add the garlic and thyme and cook for 1 minute.
Add the mushrooms, turn the heat to high, and cook, stirring, for 5 to 6 minutes until they have released their liquid and the pan is almost dry again. Season with salt and pepper.
Pour in the white wine and let it bubble and reduce by half. Pour in the stock, bring to the boil, and simmer for 15 minutes. Fish out the thyme sprigs.
Blend the soup until completely smooth. Return to the pan over gentle heat. Stir in the crème fraîche and heat through without boiling. Taste and adjust the seasoning.

items.cause: Mushrooms not cooked down properly before adding stock
items.fix: Cook the mushrooms until all their liquid has evaporated and the pan is dry before adding wine and stock. This concentrates the flavour.
Blend for at least 2 minutes in a high-powered blender. Pass through a fine sieve for an ultra-smooth result.

content.text: Velouté de champignons is standard French home cooking: a first course at autumn and winter dinner tables from Île-de-France to the Auvergne. Button mushrooms are cheap, but the finished soup is silky and rich. Swap in wild mushrooms (ceps or girolles in season) and it becomes something worthy of a restaurant.
